target_customer: Healthcare providers, pharma and researchers needing blood test results from patients at home, plus consumers
problem: Blood testing requires a clinic visit and a central lab. InnaMed's HomeLab device measured blood biomarkers at home and sent clinical reports to EMR, LIMS or EDC systems.
business_model: Hardware device plus software and clinical reports sold to providers and pharma; also raised from retail crowdfunding investors
product_category: At-home electrochemical blood testing device and analytics software

founders.name: Anup Singh
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder and CSO with no education or employers. Search summaries mention Penn and UCLA study, but that was not read in an opened source, so education is left empty.

founders.name: Eshwar Inapuri
founders.background_notes: Described as former CEO and co-founder in the Republic and KingsCrowd campaign pages and a Medium interview titled as such. Not listed on the YC page. Background not read from an opened source.

exit.reason: Fluxergy acquired some employees and assets and licensed the HomeLab technology. No reason for the wind down was found.

competitors.name: NOWDiagnostics
competitors.what: Fingertip prick point-of-care blood testing system
competitors.traction_then: FDA approved product described as a step above Theranos

competitors.name: Cor
competitors.what: In-home blood testing device positioned as general wellness
competitors.traction_then: Awaiting FDA approval as of May 2017

competitors.name: Athelas
competitors.what: Low cost home blood diagnostics device launched August 2017, about five months after the batch ended

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team had to build an electrochemical biosensor, a consumer device and analytics software while meeting clinical accuracy expectations. Theranos had just damaged trust in the category.

defensibility.rationale: Biosensor technology and any clearances would be hard to copy, but the company had no stated clearance in the sources found and the HOMELAB trademark was only registered in 2022.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it. A small diagnostics firm, Fluxergy, took some assets and employees and licensed the technology in March 2023.

market_need_then: Demand for decentralized testing was visible in 2016 and 2017 as many startups chased point-of-care and at-home tests, though the Theranos collapse made investors and regulators cautious.

identity.logo: not described in any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: clinical with a human care message in the product text

branding.brand_signature: HomeLab device name, registered as a trademark in January 2022
branding.community_and_virality: Retail crowdfunding drew over 2,400 investors on Republic in 2019, which shows some public following.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press about the brand itself. The crowdfunding community was the main sign of public interest.

outcome_analysis: InnaMed built a hard hardware and biosensor product for at-home testing and funded itself through YC, then small crowdfunding rounds on Republic in 2019 and Wefunder in 2021. In March 2023 Fluxergy took some employees and assets and licensed the HomeLab technology, which ended the company as an independent business. The company has not published why it wound down, so the cause is not public and no failure factor is assigned.
notes: Company site returned HTTP 525 on fetch. Round types are retail crowdfunding, labelled other because no source states a stage. CB Insights reports $2.43M raised over 7 rounds and a $1.22M May 2021 note; the 2021 figure rests on CB Insights plus the Wefunder page, whose SAFE totals differ ($2.2M in SAFEs). KingsCrowd shows a $12M cap for 2019 and $25M for 2021, not recorded as post money. Rounds before 2019 are missing from the total. Dealroom and KingsCrowd list closed in 2019, which conflicts with the 2023 Fluxergy deal.
